turns.content: ESPRESSO reaches apparent V<17 and HIRES reaches V<16. With observatory latitudes -24.6 and +19.8 degrees and only horizon visibility required, determine the joint magnitude cutoff and common declination interval.
Classify Stars 1 and 2 against both requirements. Star 1 has DEC=-75 degrees and absolute V=15.5 at 10 pc; Star 2 has DEC=+55 degrees and apparent V=16.5.
Classify Star 3, whose DEC is +48 degrees and supplied apparent V magnitude is 15.5. Its distance and E(B-V) are also listed, but distinguish whether they should modify an already apparent magnitude.
For Star 4 (DEC=-48 degrees, M_V=15.5, d=10 pc, E(B-V)=0.4) and Star 5 (DEC=+60 degrees, M_V=16.5, d=5 pc), compute apparent magnitudes as needed and classify both.
Assemble the all-and-only set meeting both brightness and visibility requirements, stating why each excluded star fails.
Audit Star 3 specifically against the supplied apparent magnitude and common declination interval.
Reconcile all five classifications so no star satisfying only one requirement is included.
Perform a final numerical check against V<16 and the common declination interval.
Report the stars detectable by both instruments and summarize the two tests.
